chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, brother of Udaym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says, 'O Allah, O Allah' ten times, it will be said to him, 'At your service, what is your need?'

key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service / I respond to you
key_terms.يَا اللَّهُ: O Allah (vocative form of the divine name)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying 'Ya Allah' ten times?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the efficacy of invoking the supreme divine name 'Allah' as a means of direct communion, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the power of specific divine names (Asma al-Husna) in facilitating answered prayers. The response 'At your service' (Labbayk) underscores God's immediate attentiveness to the supplicant's intent, a concept deeply rooted in the tradition of the Imams. This practice aligns with the broader theological understanding that sincere invocation of the Divine Name invites a tangible spiritual and practical response.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ayoub Bin Al Hurr, a brother of Adeym,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who says, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’, ten times, it would be said to him: ‘At your service, what is your need?’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Y ahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr brother of ‘Udaym from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever says, ‘O Allah, ten times, it will be said to him, ‘ Labbayka ’ (your call for help is well heard and noted). What kind of help do you need?”’
